column1: # Command-tree duplicates — ACKNOWLEDGED BACKLOG, not approved shapes.
# `the_command_tree_has_no_duplicate_names` asserts that no name repeats at any level of the command
# tree. A duplicated or reparented block still parses as valid TOML and still builds, so nothing else
# catches it — a real corruption of pulumi.toml (a replacement region whose end index matched an
# earlier occurrence, duplicating a span) survived a fully green suite until it was noticed by eye.
# The guard found these on its first run. They are PRE-EXISTING and UNREVIEWED: each is a second
# declaration of a name that already exists, so one of the two is dead weight and which one wins
# depends on lowering order. `aws sts` is the clearest example — one block declares an explicit
# `get-caller-identity` nested sub, another declares `first_arg` globs, and only one survives.
# Listing a row here says "known, not yet triaged". It does NOT say the shape is correct. Removing
# rows as they are resolved is the point; the guard blocks anything NOT listed, which is what stops
# a fresh corruption from slipping through the way the pulumi one did.
